summary: Unit 4 discussed cell replication and division through the process of mitosis, the creation of genetically identical cells. Topic 5.1 starts Unit 5 with a discussion of the process organisms use to reproduce sexually and maintain genetic diversity within their populations: meiosis.

vocab.definition: Segments of DNA that carry the instructions for building proteins or functional RNA molecules, acting as the fundamental units of heredity
A biological process where a single parent organism creates one or more genetically identical offspring, known as clones
A biological process that produces new, genetically unique offspring by combining genetic material from two parents
Pairs of chromosomes within a diploid cell that share the same size, shape, and gene locations, but may carry different versions (alleles) of those genes
Any chromosome that is not a sex chromosome
A type of chromosome involved in determining an individual's sex; in humans X or Y
Any cell of a living organism other than the reproductive cells
A mature haploid cell which is able to unite with another of the opposite sex in sexual reproduction to form a zygote
Contains two complete sets of chromosomes, one inherited from each parent (46 chromosomes in humans)
Contains one complete set of chromosomes, representing half the genetic material of a typical eukaryotic cell (23 chromosomes in humans)
A type of cell division in sexually reproducing organisms that produces gametes with half the number of chromosomes as the parent cell, resulting in genetically unique, haploid cells
The biological process where a male gamete (sperm) and a female gamete (egg) fuse to form a single cell called a zygote, initiating the development of a new individual
The fusion of chromosome pairs at the start of meiosis
A biological process in meiosis where homologous chromosomes exchange genetic material, creating recombinant chromosomes with a mix of genes from both parents
The randomness and separation of homologous chromosomes in meiosis 1, increasing genetic variation
The principle that any given sperm can fertilize any given egg, resulting in an enormous number of unique genetic combinations in sexually reproducing organisms
The process of cell division where one cell divides into two genetically identical daughter cells
